newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania rejects selloff of large Savings Bank.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania rejects selloff of large Savings Bank.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said on Friday that the government had no immediate plans to privatize the large state-run Savings Bank.
In terms of assets, Savings Bank is the second-largest of all state and commercial but in share capital only sixth.
Shemeta earlier announced that the government would sell the state-owned State Commercial Bank before the end of the year.
Bank privatization is a key part of an $80 million agreement between Lithuania and the World Bank.
"The privatization question of the Savings Bank is not on the government's agenda today," Shemeta told a news conference.
"It will be addressed in the future," he added.
Shemeta said that one bank was necessary to carry out the state's business and obligations.
Savings Bank had share capital at the end of 1996 of 40 million litas and 1.184 billion litas in assets.
Shemeta also said that the state-run Agricultural Bank, another top bank, would be privatized later.
"The preparatory stage for the privatization of the Agriculture Bank will begin at the end of this year or the start of next," he said.
The bank sector is recovering from a crisis which erupted in late 1995 with the surprise closure of two of the country's top banks, Innovation and Litimpeks.
Litimpeks has since been reopened and is looking for investors while Innovation is to be liquidated.
